content.text:
Good data. Pattern is clear:
- **03, 05, 06** (text only) — pure false positives passing all filters
- **01** (extra text) — real woodcut but bounding box grabbed adjacent text
- **00, 04** (little extra) — real woodcuts with minor artifacts

The most likely cause of 03/05/06: with a 20px dilation kernel, inter-line whitespace (maybe 10-15px gaps) gets bridged, merging multiple text lines into one tall blob that clears the `text_height_multiplier` filter.

The key discriminator I'd add: **horizontal regularity** — within a candidate's bounding box, what fraction of rows have below-average ink? Text blocks have regular empty rows (inter-line gaps). Woodcuts have more continuous ink distribution. Let me add this as a scored metric with debug output so we can see the actual values before committing to a threshold.
